# netactuate_router_vrf_interface (Resource)

Beta. The cloud router family is in beta: behaviour and schema may change. Manages an interface in a cloud router VRF. An ethernet interface needs a hardware id issued by NetActuate support.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netactuate_router_vrf_interface" "example" {
  name      = "example"
  router_id = 12345
  type      = "dummy"
  vrf_id    = 12345
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the interface.
- `router_id` (Number) The ID of the cloud router.
- `type` (String) The type of interface. Valid values: dummy, loopback, wireguard, ethernet.
- `vrf_id` (Number) The ID of the VRF.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description for the interface.
- `ethernet_hardware_id` (String) When creating a new ethernet interface, you must provide the Hardware ID NetActuate support provided you.
- `ipv4_cidr` (String) An IPv4 address to apply to the interface in CIDR notation (e.g., 192.0.2.1/24).
- `ipv6_cidr` (String) An IPv6 address to apply to the interface in CIDR notation.
- `wireguard_port` (Number) The port to use if this is a wireguard interface. Must be between 1 and 65535.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `interface_id` (Number) The ID of the interface.
- `wireguard_public_key` (String) The WireGuard public key of this interface (router-generated). Use this as the peer public key when configuring the remote end of the tunnel.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import netactuate_router_vrf_interface.example 12345
```
